descriptors.concept_name: Non-Current Assets and Disposal Groups Classified as Held for Sale
descriptors.definition: Entities must present non-current assets and disposal groups held for sale separately from other assets and liabilities in the balance sheet without offsetting them. Major classes of these assets and liabilities require separate disclosure, and cumulative income or expense in other comprehensive income must be presented distinctly.
inclusion: Separate balance sheet presentation of assets and liabilities
Separate presentation of cumulative OCI items
Disclosure of major classes of assets and liabilities
exclusion: Offsetting assets and liabilities of a disposal group as a single net amount
Re-presentation of comparative balance sheet amounts for prior periods
nearby_distinctions: Differs from standard non-current asset presentation by requiring distinct balance sheet grouping and specific measurement rules.

descriptors.definition: Financial statements must display non-current assets and disposal groups held for sale in a manner that allows users to evaluate their financial effects. Assets and liabilities within a disposal group must be shown separately without netting them against each other.
inclusion: Separate presentation of held for sale assets
Separate presentation of held for sale liabilities
exclusion: Netting off disposal group assets against liabilities
nearby_distinctions: Focuses specifically on balance sheet arrangement and layout rules rather than measurement or note disclosure.

descriptors.definition: Entities must provide comprehensive notes detailing the description, facts, circumstances, and expected timing of disposal for assets or disposal groups classified as held for sale. Additional required disclosures include recognized gains or losses, operating segment information, and the operational impacts of any cancelled sale plans.
inclusion: Descriptions of non-current assets or disposal groups
Circumstances and timing of expected disposal
Segment reporting classifications
exclusion: Face of balance sheet line-item values
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from balance sheet presentation by requiring qualitative descriptive narratives and supplementary details within the notes.

descriptors.definition: A discontinued operation is a component of an entity that has either been disposed of or classified as held for sale and represents a separate major line of business or geographical area. It can also be part of a single coordinated disposal plan or represent an exclusive resale-oriented subsidiary acquisition.
inclusion: Disposed components representing major lines of business
Components classified as held for sale under a coordinated plan
Subsidiaries acquired exclusively for resale
exclusion: Operations merely winding down existing contracts while continuing revenue-earning activities
Ongoing core operations without a formal disposal plan
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from general asset sales because it requires the component to represent a separate major line of business or distinct geographical area.

descriptors.definition: A discontinued operation is defined as a component of an entity that is disposed of or classified as held for sale, provided it constitutes a separate major line of business or geographic area. It also encompasses subsidiaries acquired exclusively with a view to resale.
inclusion: Major operating segments disposed of or held for sale
Geographically distinct operational areas
Subsidiaries acquired solely for resale
exclusion: Minor business units that do not constitute a major line of business
Wind-down phases where revenue earning continues normally
nearby_distinctions: Narrower than general asset disposals, applying strictly to significant operational components or major segments.

descriptors.definition: Entities must separate discontinued operations from continuing operations in financial reports to help users evaluate future cash generation capabilities. Prior period comparative figures must be re-presented to reflect operations discontinued by the end of the latest reporting period.
inclusion: Post-tax profit or loss of discontinued operations
Post-tax fair value or disposal gains and losses
Re-presentation of prior comparative periods
exclusion: Merging discontinued operational metrics directly into continuing operational totals
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on comparative restatements and segregating past performance from continuing business lines.

descriptors.concept_name: Presentation in the Statement of Profit and Loss
descriptors.definition: The statement of profit and loss must feature a single composite amount representing post-tax results of discontinued operations combined with post-tax disposal or fair value remeasurement gains. An accompanying breakdown of revenues, expenses, pre-tax results, and related income taxes must be provided either on the face or in the notes.
inclusion: Single line item for discontinued operations results
Detailed revenue and expense breakdown
Attributable income disclosures for parent owners
exclusion: Detailed line-item breakdown for newly acquired subsidiaries meeting held-for-sale criteria on acquisition
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between the aggregate single-line disclosure on the income statement face and the detailed supporting analysis.

descriptors.concept_name: Disclosures in the Statement of Cash Flows
descriptors.definition: Entities must disclose net operating, investing, and financing cash flows attributable to discontinued operations either within the financial statements or notes. Earnings per share figures for discontinued operations must also be presented with equal prominence alongside continuing operations.
inclusion: Net cash flows of discontinued operations
Basic and diluted earnings per share for discontinued operations
exclusion: Cash flow disclosures for newly acquired subsidiaries meeting held-for-sale criteria at acquisition
nearby_distinctions: Extends reporting requirements beyond the income statement to cash flow tracking and per-share performance metrics.

descriptors.definition: Basic and diluted earnings per share metrics for discontinued operations must be disclosed separately in the statement of profit and loss or notes. These figures are presented alongside continuing operations metrics with equal prominence.
inclusion: Basic EPS for discontinued operations
Diluted EPS for discontinued operations
exclusion: Combining discontinued EPS directly into a single blended EPS total without separate disclosure
nearby_distinctions: Applies per-share calculation rules distinctively to discontinued segments rather than aggregate company performance alone.

descriptors.definition: Current period adjustments directly linked to prior period discontinued operations must be classified separately within discontinued operations with disclosed natures and amounts. Such adjustments typically arise from resolving transaction purchase prices, indemnifications, or retained environmental, warranty, and employee benefit obligations.
inclusion: Resolution of purchase price uncertainties
Indemnification and warranty settlements
Employee benefit plan settlements directly tied to the disposal
exclusion: Adjustments unrelated to the original disposal transaction or prior component operations
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from normal current-year operating adjustments by their retrospective origin tied directly to historical discontinued transactions.

descriptors.concept_name: Change to a Plan of Sale
descriptors.definition: When an entity abandons its held-for-sale classification for a component, it must reclassify prior results previously shown under discontinued operations into income from continuing operations for all presented periods. The prior amounts must be clearly described as re-presented.
inclusion: Reclassification of historical operational results
Updating all presented comparative periods
exclusion: Keeping historical results categorized under discontinued operations after a sale plan is cancelled
nearby_distinctions: Applies when operational intent reverses, requiring retrospective reclassification rather than prospective adjustments.

descriptors.definition: Entities committed to sale plans that involve losing control over a subsidiary must disclose relevant discontinued operation information when the subsidiary qualifies as a disposal group. This ensures transparent reporting of structural changes affecting group composition.
inclusion: Disclosures for subsidiaries meeting discontinued operation criteria upon losing control
exclusion: Subsidiary sales that do not result in a loss of control or fail to meet the definition of a discontinued operation
nearby_distinctions: Focuses specifically on ownership control loss events rather than standard asset sales or internal operational restructuring.
